accepted.evidence: Turner 43 gives Lahnda akkh “eye” and Awankari akh with plural -iã̄ under ákṣi. Grierson Khetrani akʰī̃ has the same eye stem, with source final nasalization retained. Exact digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 5228 gives Lahnda jibbh and Awankari jībh “tongue” under jihvā́. Grierson Khetrani jībʰ exactly matches the latter local consonant and vowel pattern. Exact digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 11158 gives Lahnda lohā “iron” and Awankari lōˋā under lōhá. Grierson Khetrani lōhā has the same material sense and stem. Exact digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 2387 gives Lahnda uṭṭh “camel” under úṣṭra. Grierson Khetrani uṭʰ has the same local camel sense; the source does not mark the geminate. Exact digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 4054 gives Punjabi gadhā “ass” beside Lahnda gaḍḍãh under gardabhá. Grierson Khetrani gadʰā shares the nearby Indo-Aryan donkey form and exact sense. Exact digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.
